items.title: Understanding Digestion in Humans
items.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth where teeth break down food into smaller pieces through mechanical digestion. Saliva contains digestive juices that further break down complex components like starch into simpler sugars, making food easier to swallow and absorb.

items.title: The Role of Saliva
items.explanation: Saliva moistens food, softens it for swallowing, and chemically breaks down carbohydrates such as starch into simple sugars, which are then absorbed by the body.
